title: Make setup warn when Cargo's bin directory is not on PATH
summary: Setup's final "Ready" summary (xtask setup) will say when `${CARGO_HOME:-~/.cargo}/bin` is not on the caller's PATH, and give the line to add, so the README's `cargo test` step works on a clean machine. Audience: a new user running ./setup.sh; fix lives in xtask/src/main.rs, mirroring the existing ~/.local/bin PATH warning.

defaults_applied.how: Fix is in Rust (xtask) with minimal shell.
Unit tests for PATH helper; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check the warning text appears only when the directory is absent.
One focused change to setup output.
Detect on the user's original PATH, not setup.sh's modified one.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The warning is printed by xtask setup (not setup.sh), since PATH there reflects the user's shell, which setup.sh's internal PATH prepend does not alter; the check must use the original caller PATH. Caveat: setup.sh prepends cargo's bin to PATH before exec, so xtask would see it as present; setup.sh must therefore pass the original state (e.g. an env var) or do the check itself.
Warning only, no modification of shell profiles (rustup run with --no-modify-path).
Applies in --ci mode too only if cheap; default is printing in the non-CI Ready summary and in CI path equally.

acceptance_criteria.text: xtask/src/main.rs has a pure helper that decides whether a given directory is in a given PATH value (using split_paths), with unit tests covering present, absent, and unset PATH; the cargo bin directory is derived from CARGO_HOME or HOME/.cargo.

When Cargo's bin directory is not on PATH, the setup output (in the Ready step, shown even though setup.sh only prepends it to its own process) names the directory and the exact `export PATH=...` line to add; when it is on PATH, nothing extra is printed.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`: all tests pass, including the new PATH-detection tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
A reader following the README on a clean machine is told by setup output how to make `cargo test` work; the README's setup wording is consistent with this if touched.

out_of_scope: Other findings in the acceptance review (n4, n5, n7)
departures: setup.sh prepends cargo's bin to PATH before handing off, so the check needs the original PATH; this adds some risk beyond the reference.
